final_message:
I fixed the bug. `record_failure` in `billing/dunning.py` passed `invoice["final_action"]` to `mark_uncollectible` instead of `invoice["id"]`. That is where the `KeyError: 'final_action'` came from. It only happened when retries ran out on an invoice whose subscription was already canceled (or had no subscription). The `cancel` branch further down already passed `invoice["id"]`, so I made this line match it.

I added your test to `tests/test_lifecycle.py`, and the full suite passes (25 tests). I also wrote `answer.json` in the repository root:

```json
{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}
```

steps.command:
sed -i 's/mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice\["final_action"\])/mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice["id"])/' billing/dunning.py && echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_lifecycle.py <<'EOF'


def test_retries_exhausted_after_cancel_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [1], "final_action": "mark_unpaid"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="0002")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.engine.cancel(sub["id"], at_period_end=False)
    w.advance_days(1)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
git status --short; grep -n "mark_uncollectible" billing/dunning.py; ls answer.json
